result.topic_en: The final page (p. 210) of E555 uses the substitution sin Φ = 1/2 (Φ = 30°) to express the sum of the series as two definite integrals equal to π/sin nπ, with two corollaries in λ; the facing page 211 begins the next paper, on criteria for whether f xx + g yy = h zz is solvable.
result.transcription:
210
Multiplicetur per $d\Phi\,\text{fin.}\Phi^{-2n}\cos.\Phi$ et integretur, erit
$\int d\Phi\,\text{fin.}\Phi^{-2n}\,\text{fin.}\,2n\Phi = \frac{n}{1(1-n)}\,\text{fin.}\Phi^{2-2n}$
$+\frac{n(1-n)(1+n)}{1.2.3(2-n)}\,2^{2}\,\text{fin.}\Phi^{4-2n}+$ etc.
Statuatur pariter, integratione abfoluta, $\text{fin.}\Phi=\frac{1}{2}$, feu $\Phi=30^{\circ}$,
ac prodibit feries $Q=2^{2-2n}[?]\int d\Phi\,\text{fin.}\Phi^{-2n}\,\text{fin.}\,2n\Phi$.
Quocirca feriei propofitae fumma ita exprimetur, vt fit
$s=2^{2n+1}\int d\Phi\,\text{fin.}\Phi^{2n-1}\cos.(1-2n)\Phi$
$+2^{2-2n}[?]\int d\Phi\,\text{fin.}\Phi^{-2n}\,\text{fin.}\,2n\Phi$
et quia haec fumma iam aliunde eft cognita, habebitur
$\frac{\pi}{\text{fin.}\,n\pi}=4\int d\Phi\cos.(1-2n)\Phi\,(2\,\text{fin.}\Phi)^{2n-1}$
$+4\int d\Phi\,\text{fin.}\,2n\Phi\,(2\,\text{fin.}\Phi)^{-2n}$.
Corollarium 1.
§. 58. Si ponatur $2n=\frac{1-\lambda}{2}$, erit $1-2n=\frac{1+\lambda}{2}$,
qua pofitione noftra aequatio fit concinnior, eritque
$\frac{\pi}{\text{fin.}\frac{1-\lambda}{4}\pi}=4\int\frac{d\Phi\cos.\frac{1+\lambda}{2}\Phi}{(2\,\text{fin.}\Phi)^{\frac{1+\lambda}{2}}}+4\int\frac{d\Phi\,\text{fin.}\frac{1-\lambda}{2}\Phi}{(2\,\text{fin.}\Phi)^{\frac{1-\lambda}{2}}}=\frac{\pi\sqrt{2}}{\cos.\frac{\lambda\pi}{4}-\text{fin.}\frac{\lambda\pi}{4}}$
pofito poft integrationem $\Phi=30^{\circ}$.
Corollarium 2.
§. 59. Simili modo fumto $\lambda$ negatiue, erit
$\frac{\pi}{\text{fin.}\frac{1+\lambda}{4}\pi}=4\int\frac{d\Phi\cos.\frac{1-\lambda}{2}\Phi}{(2\,\text{fin.}\Phi)^{\frac{1-\lambda}{2}}}+4\int\frac{d\Phi\,\text{fin.}\frac{1+\lambda}{2}\Phi}{(2\,\text{fin.}\Phi)^{\frac{1+\lambda}{2}}}=\frac{\pi\sqrt{2}}{\cos.\frac{\lambda\pi}{4}+\text{fin.}\frac{\lambda\pi}{4}}$

CRITERIIS AEQVATIONIS
$fxx+gyy=hzz$
VTRVM EA RESOLVTIONEM ADMITTAT
NEC NE?
§. 1.
Notum eft huiusmodi aequationem, pro varia relatione, quae inter numeros $f$, $g$ et $h$ intercedit, modo effe poffibilem modo impoffibilem, fiquidem pro $x$, $y$ et $z$ numeros rationales accipi oporteat; atque adeo integros, quia fracti faciillime ad integros reuocarentur. Ita notum eft hanc aequationem: $xx+yy=2zz$ effe poffibilem; hanc vero: $xx+yy=3zz$ impoffibilem. Quando autem litterae $f$, $g$ et $h$ maiores tenent valores, iudicium, vtrum aequatio fit poffibilis nec ne, difficulter inftituitur; in maximis vero numeris vix fufcipiendum videtur. Hic igitur conftitui in certa criteria inquirere, ex quibus iudicare liceat, vtrum haec aequatio fit poffibilis nec ne, quantumuis magni fuerint numeri $f$, $g$ et $h$.
§. 2. Ante omnia autem fequentia notaffe iuuabit:
I°. Numeros $f$, $g$ et $h$ non folum integros affumo, fed etiam non-quadratos, neque etiam per quadratum diuifibiles;

items.english: Here, therefore, I have decided to search for definite criteria from which one can judge whether this equation is possible or not, however large the numbers f, g and h may be.

items.english: Thus it is known that the equation xx + yy = 2zz is possible, but xx + yy = 3zz is impossible.
